vector_name: ASIL B threshold boundary at exactly 90%
computation: STEP 1: Check the fault distribution: 50 + 50 + 100 + 800 = 1000 FIT. STEP 2: SPFM = 1 - (lambda_SPF + lambda_RF) / lambda_total. STEP 3: SPFM = 1 - (50 + 50) / 1000. STEP 4: SPFM = 1 - 100/1000 = 0.90. STEP 5: SPFM = 90%. STEP 6: 90% >= 90%, so ASIL B is met. STEP 7: 90% < 97% and 90% < 99%, so ASIL C and D are not met.
discriminates: THRESHOLD-BOUNDARY case: lands exactly on the ASIL B SPFM target of 90%. ISO 26262-5 Table 4 gives ≥90% for B, ≥97% for C, and ≥99% for D. ([Kekaoxing][1])
known_uncertainty: The arithmetic and SPFM expression are high confidence. The test vector treats the supplied total as the sum of the four supplied fault-rate categories; that consistency assumption is explicit here.

vector_name: ASIL C threshold boundary at exactly 97%
computation: STEP 1: Check the fault distribution: 20 + 10 + 50 + 920 = 1000 FIT. STEP 2: SPFM = 1 - (20 + 10) / 1000. STEP 3: SPFM = 1 - 30/1000 = 0.97. STEP 4: SPFM = 97%. STEP 5: 97% >= 90%, so ASIL B is met. STEP 6: 97% >= 97%, so ASIL C is met. STEP 7: 97% < 99%, so ASIL D is not met.
discriminates: THRESHOLD-BOUNDARY case: lands exactly on the ASIL C SPFM target of 97%. ISO 26262-5 Table 4 gives ≥90% for B, ≥97% for C, and ≥99% for D. ([Kekaoxing][1])
known_uncertainty: The arithmetic is exact. The vector assumes the four fault categories exhaust the stated total.

vector_name: ASIL D threshold boundary at exactly 99%
computation: STEP 1: Check the fault distribution: 5 + 5 + 20 + 970 = 1000 FIT. STEP 2: SPFM = 1 - (5 + 5) / 1000. STEP 3: SPFM = 1 - 10/1000 = 0.99. STEP 4: SPFM = 99%. STEP 5: 99% >= 90%, 97%, and 99%. STEP 6: ASIL B, C, and D targets are all met.
discriminates: THRESHOLD-BOUNDARY case: lands exactly on the ASIL D SPFM target of 99%, distinguishing equality handling from a strict-greater-than implementation. ([Kekaoxing][1])
known_uncertainty: The arithmetic is exact. The vector assumes the four fault categories sum to the stated total.

computation: STEP 1: Convert temperatures: T_use = 55 + 273 = 328 K; T_stress = 125 + 273 = 398 K. STEP 2: Arrhenius acceleration factor AF = exp[(Ea/k) × (1/T_use - 1/T_stress)]. STEP 3: AF = exp[(0.7/8.6e-5) × (1/328 - 1/398)] = 78.615. STEP 4: Point FIT estimate = failures × 10^9 / (device-hours × AF) = 15 × 10^9 / (1,000,000 × 78.615) = 190.803 FIT. STEP 5: At 60% confidence with 15 failures, the JESD85 chi-square upper-bound calculation uses χ² = 33.4 and 2f+2 = 32 degrees of freedom. STEP 6: FIT_60% = 33.4 × 10^9 / (2 × 1,000,000 × 78.615) = 212.306 FIT. STEP 7: Rounded values are 190.8 FIT point estimate and 212.3 FIT upper confidence bound.
discriminates: Realistic mid-range JESD85-style case using the standard's published 0.7 eV, 55 degrees C use, 125 degrees C stress example and a substantial 1,000,000 device-hour exposure. The reproduced JESD85A material reports AF approximately 78.6 for these Arrhenius inputs. ([Scribd][2])
known_uncertainty: The Arrhenius calculation is sensitive to the temperature convention and activation energy. JESD85A notes that junction temperature may need to replace ambient temperature when self-heating is material. ([Scribd][2])

vector_name: 15 failures, 90% confidence, same exposure with higher confidence bound
computation: STEP 1: T_use = 55 + 273 = 328 K; T_stress = 125 + 273 = 398 K. STEP 2: AF = exp[(0.7/8.6e-5) × (1/328 - 1/398)] = 78.615. STEP 3: Point FIT = 15 × 10^9 / (1,000,000 × 78.615) = 190.803 FIT. STEP 4: For 90% confidence and 15 failures, use χ² = 42.6 with 2f+2 = 32 degrees of freedom. STEP 5: FIT_90% = 42.6 × 10^9 / (2 × 1,000,000 × 78.615) = 270.844 FIT. STEP 6: Rounded values are 190.8 FIT point estimate and 270.8 FIT upper confidence bound.
discriminates: Confidence-level case: the physical test exposure and acceleration factor are unchanged from the first vector, so only the confidence-bound calculation changes. The JESD85A example uses the same Arrhenius setup and gives the corresponding chi-square method. ([Scribd][2])
known_uncertainty: The exact chi-square quantile depends on the standard's stated degrees-of-freedom convention and confidence convention. The value 42.6 is the rounded value used in the reproduced JESD85A worked material.

computation: STEP 1: T_use = 55 + 273 = 328 K; T_stress = 125 + 273 = 398 K. STEP 2: AF = exp[(0.5/8.6e-5) × (1/328 - 1/398)] = 22.591. STEP 3: Point FIT = 0 × 10^9 / (2,000,000 × 22.591) = 0 FIT. STEP 4: With zero failures, 2f+2 = 2 degrees of freedom. STEP 5: The 90% chi-square quantile for 2 degrees of freedom is 4.60517. STEP 6: FIT_90% = 4.60517 × 10^9 / (2 × 2,000,000 × 22.591) = 50.963 FIT. STEP 7: Thus zero observed failures gives a zero point estimate but a nonzero upper confidence bound.
discriminates: Degenerate statistical boundary: zero failures. It tests that the calculator does not confuse a zero point estimate with a zero upper confidence bound. The Arrhenius setup is also a published JESD85A example for 0.5 eV, for which AF is approximately 22.6. ([Scribd][2])
known_uncertainty: JEDEC FIT calculations are statistical rather than regulatory-threshold calculations; unlike ISO SPFM and EAR TPP, there is no regulatory FIT limit in this vector. The confidence-bound convention should be implemented exactly as specified by the selected JESD85 revision.

computation: STEP 1: Under the EAR Technical Note, TPP = 2 × MacTOPS × bit length, and 2 × MacTOPS may correspond to reported TOPS. Therefore for reported TOPS = 600 at 8 bits, TPP = 600 × 8. STEP 2: TPP = 4800. STEP 3: Compare 4800 with the 3A090.a.1 threshold of 4800. STEP 4: 4800 >= 4800, so the vector is on the controlled side of the 3A090.a.1 threshold.
discriminates: THRESHOLD-BOUNDARY case: exactly reaches the current 3A090.a.1 TPP threshold of 4800. BIS's Technical Note gives 600 tera integer operations at 8 bits as an example producing TPP 4800. ([Federal Register Public Inspection][3])
known_uncertainty: This vector assumes the supplied TOPS figure corresponds to 2 × MacTOPS as contemplated by the EAR Technical Note. The regulation also requires the maximum theoretically possible MacTOPS and, where multiple bit lengths apply, evaluation of the highest TPP. ([Eccn][4])

computation: STEP 1: TPP = reported TOPS × bit width = 599 × 8. STEP 2: TPP = 4792. STEP 3: Compare 4792 with 4800. STEP 4: 4792 < 4800, so this vector is 8 TPP below the 3A090.a.1 threshold.
discriminates: ADJACENT-THRESHOLD case: changes only one TOPS unit from the preceding vector and moves from exactly 4800 to 4792, testing strict versus inclusive threshold handling. The current 3A090.a.1 threshold is 4800 or more. ([Federal Register Public Inspection][3])
known_uncertainty: The arithmetic is exact under the reported-TOPS interpretation. Actual ECCN classification can require applying the other 3A090 notes and definitions, so this vector tests the numerical TPP parameter rather than complete export-control classification.

vector_name: Realistic mid-range multi-bit processor with highest TPP selected
computation: STEP 1: Mode 1 TPP = 300 × 16 = 4800. STEP 2: Mode 2 TPP = 200 × 8 = 1600. STEP 3: Select the highest applicable TPP = max(4800, 1600) = 4800. STEP 4: Compare highest TPP with the 3A090.a.1 threshold: 4800 >= 4800. STEP 5: The numerical TPP therefore reaches the 3A090.a.1 threshold. The EAR Technical Note explicitly states that when multiple bit lengths produce different TPP values, the highest TPP value should be evaluated. ([Eccn][4])

expected_output.threshold_side: highest TPP is exactly at the 3A090.a.1 threshold

discriminates: Multi-bit-width case: tests aggregation/selection of the highest TPP rather than evaluating only a nominal operating mode. The EAR Technical Note says the highest TPP should be evaluated when multiple bit lengths achieve different TPP values. ([Eccn][4])
known_uncertainty: The vector deliberately tests only the TPP parameter. Complete 3A090 treatment can additionally depend on performance density and the applicable notes; the 3A090.a.2 threshold is TPP ≥1600 together with performance density ≥5.92. ([Federal Register Public Inspection][3])
